name: glyph-anatomy
title: Glyph Anatomy
description: A word builds as in a font editor, with metric guides, anchors along each contour and Bézier handles that pull straight segments into curves before the glyphs fill.
useWhen: A product for designers, a type or a design tool should show its craft: the letters are built from points and curves on screen.
A title should feel constructed and precise, with the scaffolding visible for a moment before the clean word.
You want to show how a letter is made, for a talk, a course or a type specimen.
avoidWhen: The outline should simply draw itself without points or handles: use outline-trace.
The design-tool feel should come from a selection box around the word: use selection-snap.
The word only needs a quiet reveal: use soft-blur-in.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Text
variables.description: Word or short phrase. Letters, digits and . , ! ? ' - : & @ # $ % + / ( ) are built from Inter ExtraBold outlines; other characters become spaces.

variables.label: Glyph color
variables.description: Color of the letters and their outlines.

variables.label: Points
variables.description: Color of guides, anchors and handles.

variables.label: Font size
variables.description: Text size in reference pixels (1280×720 stage); long text shrinks to fit.

variables.label: Guides
variables.description: Show the cap height, x-height, baseline and descender lines.

variables.label: Keep points
variables.description: Leave the anchors and handles on screen after the fill.
